title: Stepwise Cell Seeding on Tessellated Scaffolds to Study Sprouting Blood Vessels
protocol: Obtain access to specialized equipment for photolithography.
Design scaffolds using the selected geometry of interest.
Prepare scaffolds using a photolithography technique.
Clean the silicon wafer using plasma cleaning or a solvent-based technique.
Spray the cleaned wafer with compressed nitrogen gas.
Inspect the wafer to ensure it is free from debris.
Center a silicon wafer onto the spin-coater chuck using a guide.
Briefly spin the wafer to ensure proper centering on the chuck, adjust as necessary.
Dispense 1-4 mL of lift-off reagent onto the wafer.
Set spin-coater spread speed at 500 rpm for 5 seconds.
Spin-speed set to 1000 rpm for 30 seconds and spin the lift-off reagent.
Inspect the wafer to ensure it has an even coating across the wafer.
Transfer the coated wafer to a hot plate and bake for 1 minute at 200 °C.
Repeat the previous steps two more times for a total of three coatings.
Spin-coat the lift-off reagent coated silicon wafer with SU-8 2050 photoresist until obtaining a thickness of approximately 100 µm.
Dispense 1 mL of resist for every 25 mm of substrate diameter.
Avoid bubbles while pouring the resist.
Pour approximately a 2-inch diameter circle when using a 4-inch silicon wafer.
Spin-coat the SU-8 2050 at a speed of 500 rpm for 5 seconds.
Increase spin speed to between 1700 to 1800 rpm to achieve approximately 100 µm thickness.
Leave the spin coated wafers to de-gas overnight on a level surface protected from light (optional).
Pre-bake the wafers at 65 °C for 10 min prior to exposure.
Continue pre-baking the wafers at 95 °C for 40-50 min after initial pre-bake.
Test the surface of the resist by pressing on the edge with a pair of tweezers before exposure to ensure it is no longer tacky/viscous.
Expose photoresist to UV light with an energy of 215-240 mJ/cm² through a photomask for resist thicknesses between 85 - 110 µm.
Calibrate exposure energy as necessary to achieve the desired value.
Adjust exposure time to ensure proper calibration and verification of energy settings.
Bake the wafer immediately after UV exposure at 65 °C for 2-5 minutes.
Continue baking the wafer at 95 °C for 8-10 minutes.
Immerse the scaffolds in SU-8 developer solution for 7-10 minutes to dissolve any undeveloped resist.
Rinse the scaffolds with isopropyl alcohol (IPA).
Dry the wafer with compressed nitrogen.
Hard bake the wafers at 150 °C for 15 min.
Submerge the scaffolds in SU-8 developer to cause them to immediately lift off the wafer.
Gently push the scaffolds with a pair of wafer-tweezers if necessary.
Remove excess developer from the scaffolds.
Transfer the scaffolds into a new container and submerge in isopropyl alcohol.
Rinse the scaffolds in IPA for a minimum of 6 times to ensure all developer has been removed.
Air dry the scaffolds for a minimum of a week before use.
Submerge the scaffolds in 70% ethanol (v/v) for a minimum of 15 minutes for disinfection.
Wash the scaffolds 2 times in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Dilute human fibronectin in PBS to prepare a 50 µg/mL solution.
Mix 1.5 µL of fibronectin stock solution (1 mg/mL) with 28.5 µL of PBS for each scaffold.
For 10 scaffolds, mix 15 µL of fibronectin stock in 285 µL of PBS to make a total of 300 µL of the dilution.
Cover each scaffold with 30 µL of the fibronectin solution prepared above.
Place scaffolds sparsely on a hydrophobic surface (non-tissue culture dish).
Incubate scaffolds at 37 °C and 100% humidity for at least one hour.
Rinse scaffolds lightly in PBS to remove any remaining fibronectin.
Store the rinsed scaffolds in PBS at 4 °C for up to a week before use.
Prepare EC medium by mixing basal medium with appropriate components including Pen/Strep, FBS, and endothelial cell growth supplements.
Make a HAMEC suspension in EC medium at a concentration of 4 x 106 cells/mL.
Place one fibronectin-coated scaffold per well on a nonTC 24-well plate well using forceps.
Cover each scaffold with 25 μL droplets of the HAMEC suspension carefully.
Avoid letting the suspension flow away from the scaffold to prevent hindering cell adhesion.
Incubate the plate in an incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2 and 100% humidity for a minimum of 60 minutes and a maximum of 90 minutes.
Place the plate on an orbital shaker within the incubator set at no more than 5 rpm during incubation to improve cell attachment onto the scaffold's walls.
After incubation, fill each well with 700 μL of EC medium using a pipette.

Incubate endothelialized scaffolds until EC confluence can be observed using fluorescent microscopy on the scaffold's walls when using labeled ECs, or for 3 days when using non-labeled ECs to achieve EC confluence.
Change the medium every other day during incubation.
Prepare dental pulp stem cell medium by mixing low-glucose DMEM, FBS, NEAA, GlutaMAX, and penicillin-streptomycin-nystatin solution.
Transfer endothelialized scaffolds into a new nonTC 24-well plate using forceps to discard ECs attached to the wells' bottom.
Discard all media from the current plate using a 1 mL pipette or vacuum suction without applying vacuum straight on the scaffold.
Place one scaffold per well at the center of each well.
Dry the area surrounding the scaffold with light vacuum but avoid complete drying of the scaffold.
Prepare a DPSC suspension in fibrin pre-gel solution by diluting thrombin and fibrinogen stock solutions with PBS to obtain final concentrations of 5 U/mL and 15 mg/mL, respectively.
Distribute 12.5 µL of said DPSC suspension per scaffold to be seeded using a pipette set to 12.5 µL.
Fill the pipette with the 15 mg/mL fibrinogen solution.
Set the pipette to 25 μL without removing the tip.
Press the plunger button until the liquid reaches the tip opening but does not leak out, then hold in this position.
Insert the pipette into a microcentrifuge tube containing cells in thrombin suspension and draw the cell suspension into the tip.
Thoroughly mix the materials to avoid bubble formation.
Quickly dispense the mixed materials on top of an endothelialized scaffold.
Replace tips between uses for each scaffold to prevent fibrin gel formation within the tip.
Incubate scaffolds at 37 °C, 5% CO2 and 100% humidity for 30 minutes.
Fill each well with 1 mL of 1:1 DPSC and EC medium after incubation.
Culture constructs for 1 week, changing medium every other day.
Image the constructs using a confocal microscope at different time points to study vascular development or any other parameter of interest.
Discard media from the wells at day 7.
Rinse the scaffolds by adding PBS to the wells and removing it using vacuum.
Fix the scaffolds by adding 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 minutes.
Wash in PBS three times, 5 minutes per wash.
Permeabilize fixed cells using 0.3% Triton-X in PBS (v/v) for 15 minutes.
Wash in PBS three times, 5 minutes per wash.
Cover scaffolds with a 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS (w/v) blocking solution.
Leave the scaffolds covered in the blocking solution at room temperature for 1 hour.
Dilute rabbit anti-von Willebrand factor (vWF) antibody 1:150 and mouse anti-SMA antibody 1:50 in fresh blocking solution.
Cover the scaffolds with the primary antibodies solution.
Keep the scaffolds covered with primary antibodies solution at 4 °C overnight.
Wash in PBS three times, 5 minutes per wash.
Prepare and apply the secondary antibodies staining solution.
Dilute goat anti-mouse Cy3 antibody 1:150 in PBS.
Dilute goat anti-rabbit Alexa-Fluor 488 1:400 in PBS.
Cover the scaffolds with the secondary antibodies solution.
Incubate for a minimum of 3 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the scaffolds three times in PBS, five minutes per wash.
Keep stained scaffold in 0.3% PFA in PBS (v/v) for up to a month.
Image the scaffolds using a confocal microscope with a 5X lens and a zoom of 0.5.
Crop each individual compartment using ImageJ or another image processing software.
Remove any vessel not located inside the compartment area.
Create a maximum intensity projection.
Save each individual cropped compartment as a TIFF image.
In ImageJ, open the TIFF image containing several compartments using File > Open.
Select the Polygon selection tool from the toolbar.
Choose the transmitted light channel.
Click on one of the corners of the hexagonal compartment at the interface between the compartment area and the scaffold wall to start defining the mask.
Continue clicking sequentially on each corner until you return to the initial corner, completing the polygon shape for the mask.
Fit the mask to follow the inner wall of the scaffold regardless of its shape (hexagonal, square, or circular).
Select Analyze > Tools > ROI manager from the menu.
In the ROI manager, click Add to save the created mask.
Save a file with all the created masks by clicking More > Save in the ROI manager and choose an appropriate name and location for the .roi file.
To retrieve saved masks, open them using More > Open in the ROI manager and select the desired .roi file.
Select the fluorescent vessel network image.
Click on Edit > Clear outside.
Duplicate the cleared network image by clicking Image > Duplicate.
Name the duplicated image in the Duplicate pop-up window.
Unselect the Duplicate hyperstack option and click OK.
Save the cropped image by clicking File > Save as > Tiff.
Choose the name and directory for the saved image and click OK.
Download and install AngioTool software.
Set the scale value of the images to obtain results in millimeter units.
Load an image into AngioTool.
Click on the Setting tab.
Fill the Distance in pixels with 400.
Fill the Distance in mm with 1.
Press the Open image button and browse for the image of interest.
Choose analysis parameters in the Analysis tab to quantify vessel development.
Deselect any present marker from the top range selector under the Vessel diameter and intensity field.
Activate the marker representing the number 3 on the top range selector.
Move the lower range marker to 60 under the bottom range selector for vessel diameter and intensity.
Leave the high range marker at 255.
Activate the Remove small particles box and set the marker to 100.
Select the name and location of the spreadsheet file in which the results will be saved.
Press the Run analysis button.
Choose to save result image if desired, generating a new jpeg image showing quantified parameters.
Organize data from processed images into a statistical analysis software.
Input parameters such as Total vessel length and Vessel area for proper study.
Set up a confocal microscope culture chamber at 37 °C, 5% CO2 and 100% humidity for time-lapse imaging.
Put the plate containing the fully seeded scaffolds in the confocal microscope chamber.
Set the imaging parameters to the desired values.
Set the image taking interval to 30 minutes and the total imaging time to 72 hours.
Save the complete time lapse movie file as a TIFF sequence.
Open ImageJ and click File > Import > Image sequence.
Select your files to open the TIFF sequence as a movie.
Open the Manual Tracking plugin by clicking on Plugins > Manual Tracking.
Observe the movie.
Select the vessel to be tracked.
Activate the Show parameters box.
Input 30 minutes for Time interval.
Press the Add track button.
On the movie's first frame, press the location of the vessel to be tracked.
Click on the image of the second frame where the vessel is located.
Proceed with clicking on each subsequent frame until full migration tracking is completed.
Click on the Overlay Dots & Lines to imprint a visual path of the vessel migration on the movie.
Click on the End Track button to finalize recording the current vessel movement.
Click on the Add track button again to start over with a new vessel.
Repeat the process until all desired vessels are tracked.
